purpose: Reusable authoring prompts for four Xonix territory-reveal game families; no prompt has been executed merely by being in this catalog.

prompts.intent: Establish Daybreak Front as the main visual identity.
prompts.prompt: Write a compact art bible for FPV FRONT, a Ukrainian FPV-drone territory-reveal arcade set in the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Main chapter: Daybreak Front; alternate chapters: Night Signal and Steel Horizon. Give each a palette with semantic roles, silhouette rules, material vocabulary, UI hierarchy, enemy-role mapping, reveal-art composition, music direction and six asset acceptance checks. Main reveal pictures must visibly contain fictional invading Russian military forces and equipment, not become landscape-only rewards. Player: practical Ukrainian FPV quadcopter with thin carbon frame, four visible propellers, compact battery and forward camera, with restrained blue/yellow identity accents, ivory silhouette and gold signal trail. Use original 1990s Amiga/16-bit visual richness with modern clarity. War scenes are fictional artistic compositions; use military vehicles and equipment as enemies. Distinguish dim vehicles in the artwork from bright, shape-coded live hazards. Specify which decisions affect presentation only and which need supported rule primitives. End with twelve chapter ideas that change atmosphere and challenges without changing player identity. Current FPV art direction: use a recognizable practical FPV silhouette rather than a toy drone icon; preserve a thin carbon frame, distinct propellers, compact battery/camera and restrained Ukrainian accents. Use no Z markings anywhere in current concepts. Ukrainian player assets, hostile military assets and neutral scenery have explicit distinct identity in the authoring brief; never put Ukrainian markings on hostile units. Military infantry, vehicles and equipment may replace abstract symbols when their existing semantic behavior remains clear. X and chevrons are temporary visual examples, not required final art. Keep the full terrain footprint visible even when a smaller decorative prop represents it. Changing visual scale or a prop never changes the logical collider or fill policy.
variations: Daybreak Front: wheat gold, olive, ink blue; rural military illustration.
Night Signal: deep navy, wet concrete, amber; fictional urban military scene.
Steel Horizon: copper, steel blue, chalk; rail yards and invading military vehicles.

prompts.prompt: Create original promotional key art for 1994 FOREVER that feels like an imaginary premium 1990s game box. A tiny ivory toy spacecraft draws a luminous right-angle path through dark space, opening an angular window onto a warm computer room at sunset. Beige plastic, turquoise, tangerine and deep violet, expressive pixel clusters, a few carefully placed stars. Framed composition with generous blank title zone at top and small empty footer. Make the central reveal understandable at thumbnail size. No existing game characters, real publishers, fake review scores, rating badges or generated text. Nostalgia comes from tactile detail and light; avoid a generic neon grid as the entire subject.

prompts.intent: Make Coupa-inspired value recovery playful and broad.
reference_requirements: Official Coupa reference notes; supplied brand assets only if available.
prompts.prompt: Write a theme bible for NAVI NETWORK, a Coupa business-spend-management and AI-inspired territory-reveal arcade. The fantasy is helping a business network work better: reconnect suppliers, align order/receipt/invoice tokens, recover fictional savings and open productive districts. Use current official Coupa reference notes {{REFERENCE_NOTES}} for terminology. Hero remains an original cobalt C-token placeholder until supplied official Navi art is selected; never invent a supposedly official Navi mascot. Define three treatments: Savings City, AI Network and Paper Circuit. Propose cobalt/mint/ivory visual roles, friendly modular UI, role-based hazards such as duplicate records, bottlenecks, exception emitters and disruption clouds. Treat employees, customers and suppliers as the world being helped. Describe six objective ideas composed from supported capture/collect/link rules. Keep gameplay points explicitly fictional; this is an arcade metaphor, not an implementation of Coupa business processes.

prompts.intent: Reveal a living business network instead of a spreadsheet.
prompts.prompt: Create one original 4:3 pixel-art reveal illustration for NAVI NETWORK: a friendly miniature business district with supplier workshops, a small market, delivery routes, warehouse roofs and illuminated office windows. Cobalt structures, ivory paving, mint connection lines inside the illustration and warm coral accents. Compose three discoveries: a workshop becoming active, a delivery bridge and a shared plaza. This is an original Coupa-inspired game concept, not an official product screenshot. No actual financial data, company logos, generated text or real dashboard interface. Keep the illustration lower-contrast than future live game sprites; mint routes must be broad subdued scene details, not bright lines easily confused with an active capture trail. Full artwork only, no fog, game borders, live hazards or HUD.
variations: Paper Circuit: folded document city with order, receipt and invoice station shapes; no text.
AI Network: elegant constellation of small helpful workshop islands joined by calm connection channels.

prompts.intent: Explore a replaceable placeholder with human-friendly character.
prompts.prompt: Design six original pixel-art avatar candidates for NAVI NETWORK, a Coupa-inspired arcade. Use a small cobalt circular token with a simple white C-like opening as the explicit placeholder direction, alongside two compact helpful guide-bot silhouettes and two folded-paper navigation tokens. None is represented as official Navi artwork. Warm friendly proportions, ivory outline, one mint accent, obvious facing notch, readable at a proposed 24–32 source pixels. Quiet navy background, consistent scale, no pseudo-official wordmarks. The token should look like an active cursor that guides a route, not a currency coin or a customer portrayed as an obstacle. Present enlarged views plus tiny silhouette tests; sprite construction and branding substitution happen later.

prompts.intent: Turn spend friction into distinct abstract obstacles.
prompts.prompt: Create a four-column pixel-art obstacle study for NAVI NETWORK, each with a tiny-size sample, enlarged shape and small route-domain diagram. Duplicate record: twin offset document blocks with a diamond center, an open-field bouncer confined to unrevealed territory. Bottleneck: a squat bar with an hourglass gap that follows the changing capture contour, including internal edges created by a cut. Rework ticket: a compact rounded document cart moving across revealed ground, with broad footprint geometry rather than a line-hugging silhouette. Scope leak: a notched paper-strip dispenser with a clearly telegraphed missing-tile footprint for proposed territory erosion. Use friendly toy-machine language, graphite cores with amber/coral accents, monochrome-readable shapes and a quiet cobalt or ivory background. The obstacles represent process friction, never customers, suppliers or employees. No military motifs, real invoice text, actual business claims or company logos. An exception emitter is a separate stationary capturable objective study, not a moving-role substitute. These are proposed visual role studies. Read the current primitive catalog before making pack bindings: enemy.bounce-field.v1 specifies the open-field bouncer and enemy.patrol-boundary.v1 specifies only the outer border. Interior-contour patrol, movement across revealed ground, and territory erosion need extensions unless a later catalog explicitly defines them. A rendered sprite does not implement a behavior. Show role status in the accompanying production brief, never as tiny baked-in image text. A shared fill-blocker mark belongs only to roles designated by the selected fill policy, not to every moving enemy. Keep a separate hollow-circle marker for capturable objectives. Add a separate three-symbol terrain key: a filled block with a barred-edge pattern for a solid wall blocking both player and enemies; spaced drag-chevron tracks for terrain that slows only the player while enemies remain unaffected; and an unmistakable hazard-cross pattern for terrain lethal to the player while enemies remain unaffected. Distinguish these by shape and texture, not color alone. Treat local slow/lethal terrain as proposed and extension-needed until the current contract supports their exact semantics; do not portray an ordinary solid wall as damaging.

prompts.intent: Create a game interface that feels clear and business-friendly.
prompts.prompt: Create a polished NAVI NETWORK menu/intermission concept in modern pixel art. Cobalt and ivory panels, mint focus rings, warm small scene illustrations. Main center card has a large empty 4:3 arena placeholder for a measured game board to be composited later. Right rail shows three blank module cards with distinct icons for preview, connection and recovery. Top status has simple life pips, captured-area meter and fictional value-points icon; omit real currency claims and fabricated KPI text. A quiet footer shows blank controller-hint slots. Original C token is a placeholder hero badge, not an official Navi mascot. Use ample spacing, large clear visual groups and subtly playful geometry, avoiding a dense enterprise dashboard. Provide visual style only; real text and focus order are separate UI work. Provide a separate compact teaching-key study outside the arena: open-field mover, patrol on an interior captured contour, mover on revealed ground, and telegraphed territory eroder. Reserve each a different silhouette and route diagram. Show solid-wall, player-only slow-terrain and lethal-terrain symbols as three distinct material/shape treatments. The teaching key is an authoring study; select only supported roles for any actual level and label absent behaviors proposed/extension-needed in the production brief. Keep real wording in localization slots. Claimed ground must not be presented as safe from every enemy class.

prompts.intent: Show a connection becoming useful when a region closes.
prompts.prompt: Create a five-panel pixel-art capture-effect storyboard for NAVI NETWORK, fixed simple rectilinear closed region and placeholder C-token endpoint. The exposed ivory route connects; a tiny mint pulse appears at closure; recovered region fills with a quiet grid of light; supplier workshop windows illuminate inside the revealed picture; the boundary settles into a calm claimed-route edge. One optional matching-token pair gives a small separate icon sparkle after capture. Keep state order explicit and all geometry identical. No exploding dollar bills, full-screen bloom or fake business metric text. Show a sixth reduced-motion keyframe with immediate reveal and steady lit windows. This still sheet is an animation brief, not actual running UI or proof of economic results. Add a clearly separate proposed victory-to-gallery inset after gameplay: freeze active hazards, reveal the complete artwork as the completion reward, and keep the actual achieved capture percentage in a separate empty score slot for real UI text. Full artwork visibility must not silently change collision geometry or report 100% captured. Ordinary capture keyframes still reveal only the region allowed by the selected fill policy. Treat the full-artwork victory presentation as a proposed UI capability until implemented; the illustration alone does not prove it exists. Use claimed boundary for the completed route rather than implying universal safety from all enemy classes.

prompts.intent: Give Coupa-inspired play a warm, confident sound.
prompts.prompt: Write an original composer brief for NAVI NETWORK. Use crisp marimba-like synth plucks, soft FM bass, restrained breakbeat and warm chord pads; make it playful and focused rather than corporate hold music. Propose one 116 BPM 64-bar loop with synchronized foundation, trail-tension and successful-connection stems. The bright closure cue should be a small upward resolution; an exception warning should remain clearly distinguishable without being harsh. Include a quieter planning/gallery arrangement and five short UI cue descriptions. Map sounds to neutral simulation event names so the same rules can use other theme packs. All value points are fictional game feedback. Output a written cue sheet and delivery specification, not fabricated audio or claims that a still image tool made music.

prompts.intent: Explain value recovery through an inviting illustrated city.
prompts.prompt: Create original landscape pixel-art promotional key art for NAVI NETWORK. A cobalt C-token placeholder traces a clean ivory right-angle route across a dark blue field, revealing a lively connected business city with supplier workshops, delivery bridges and warm office windows. Mint light spreads into recovered districts, suggesting useful connections and fictional savings. Premium playful BSM/AI-platform mood, simple hero silhouette, strong central composition and plenty of quiet upper-left space for title typography. Do not invent an official Navi mascot or Coupa wordmark. No real monetary claims, customer names, fake app screenshots or generated text. This is concept key art; future official brand assets can replace the placeholder cleanly.

prompts.intent: Make one controlled change to an accepted visual.
reference_requirements: Target image that has been opened and inspected.
Optional style reference image explicitly assigned a style-only role.
prompts.prompt: Edit the supplied target image {{TARGET_IMAGE}}. Change only {{CHANGE_REQUEST}}. Treat {{LOCKED_FEATURES}} as locked: preserve their identity, position, proportions, facing direction, palette relationship and scene composition. Use the supplied style reference {{STYLE_REFERENCE}} only for pixel clustering, material language and lighting; do not copy its layout or add its subjects. Keep existing military subjects in FPV scenes, region/period identity in Atlas scenes and placeholder status in Navi scenes. Preserve the canvas ratio and all unaffected areas as closely as the editing tool permits. Return one edited concept and report any visible drift separately. If required target/reference images are absent, identify the missing input before editing. Do not claim pixel-perfect preservation without comparison.

prompts.intent: Convert source artwork while preserving its subject.
reference_requirements: Inspected source reveal image.
prompts.prompt: Edit the supplied full reveal artwork {{TARGET_IMAGE}} into deliberate modern pixel art. Preserve every major subject, scene meaning, relative placement, crop and focal hierarchy. For FPV FRONT, keep the invading military vehicles present; do not replace them with scenic decoration. Use {{PALETTE}} and an intended {{LOGICAL_WIDTH}}-pixel art grid with controlled clusters, selective dithering in broad shading and crisp silhouette edges. Do not add fog, game lines, UI, captions, extra characters or new logos. Remove photographic microtexture while retaining recognizable materials. This is an artistic conversion concept; exact dimensions, palette count and source-grid consistency must be checked in a separate asset-production pass.

prompts.intent: Allow clean illustrated image packs behind the same pixel overlay.
reference_requirements: Inspected source reveal image.
prompts.prompt: Edit {{TARGET_IMAGE}} into a flat editorial illustration with vector-like shape language: clean contours, broad quiet color areas, two or three shading steps and sparse texture. Preserve all subject identities, relative positions, military/cultural/business context and the existing crop. {{PALETTE}} guides the colors. Keep detailed discoveries in three separated focal zones and lower local contrast around the outer margin. No gameplay overlay, UI or text. Result is a raster illustration concept, not an SVG or editable vector file. The eventual crisp pixel-art player, hazards and trail will remain separate assets above this image style.

prompts.intent: Support painterly reveal packs without muddying the game.
reference_requirements: Inspected source reveal image.
prompts.prompt: Edit {{TARGET_IMAGE}} into a luminous painterly reveal illustration using {{PAINTERLY_MEDIUM}} with broad quiet shapes and controlled texture. Keep the same objects, subjects, landmarks, military presence where applicable, composition and aspect ratio. Restrict bright small specks, soften secondary detail and retain clear large discoveries. Use {{PALETTE}} and {{LIGHTING}}. Do not paint the game HUD, fog, path, border or moving enemies into the image. Preserve a quiet margin and a medium-contrast base so a separately drawn crisp arcade overlay remains legible. Output one artwork concept; do not claim that a painterly image has become a pixel-art sprite or a layered source document.
variations: PAINTERLY_MEDIUM = transparent watercolor with reserved paper highlights
PAINTERLY_MEDIUM = opaque gouache with dry-brush edges
PAINTERLY_MEDIUM = softly textured oil-paint illustration

prompts.intent: Support photographic or cinematic reveal styling as a separate layer.
reference_requirements: Inspected source artwork; metadata stating generated versus real source.
prompts.prompt: Edit {{TARGET_IMAGE}} into a carefully composed {{PHOTO_TREATMENT}} reveal artwork. Preserve source subjects, locations as represented, object placement and crop; retain fictional invading military equipment in FPV art. For an invented military scene the result must remain described in metadata as fictional generated art, not documentary evidence. Use broad natural light, restrained highlights and modest depth separation without dissolving key objects into blur. Remove only distracting microtexture requested by the edit brief. No game UI, crosshairs, coordinates, tactical annotations, active hazards or reveal mask. The game overlay remains pixel art and is composited separately. Produce a concept image, not claims of real-event accuracy.
variations: PHOTO_TREATMENT = cinematic miniature-diorama photography
PHOTO_TREATMENT = warm analog-film-inspired still life
PHOTO_TREATMENT = realistic architectural illustration with photographic lighting

prompts.intent: Turn a supplied picture into a traceable pack candidate.
reference_requirements: Actual source file.
Current pack schema and authoritative overlay fixture, when available.
prompts.prompt: Prepare {{SOURCE_FILE}} as a candidate reveal-image asset using the current workspace authoring skill and pack schema. Inspect source dimensions, color mode, orientation and visible content first. Preserve the original. Propose a normalized 4:3 crop and record focal anchors in normalized coordinates; if the requested crop removes the main subject, supply a contain/letterbox alternative. Create a preview with the existing authoritative overlay fixture, keeping simulation geometry unchanged. Record intended sampling, background dimming/underlay settings, source attribution/provenance, content tags, gallery caption and asset status. Execute only supported authorized asset actions; use the active image-editing tool for artistic edits and explicit asset-production tools for requested exports. Do not invent missing image files or mark the candidate as runtime-tested. Deliver source/candidate paths and observed validation results.

prompts.intent: Describe states before asking for frames.
reference_requirements: Accepted character image inspected at actual-size target.
Role semantics and existing animation contract if available.
prompts.prompt: Using the accepted {{CHARACTER_REFERENCE}} and behavior role {{ROLE}}, write a sprite-state specification for a cardinal-movement territory game. Include idle, north/east/south/west movement, exposed-trail state, hit, invulnerability, ability-ready and victory, only where meaningful. Propose a fixed frame canvas and common pivot; distinguish decorative extent from collision geometry, which remains owned by the simulation. For each animation give tag, facing policy, frame count, frame duration, loop direction and invariant silhouette features. Explain whether movement facings are drawn or transformed and how to preserve lighting. Include a low-motion option. Output a table and metadata draft, not a sprite image or assurance that generated frames will align.

prompts.intent: Explore one animation without redesigning the character.
reference_requirements: Inspected accepted sprite reference.
State specification giving frame count and motion.
prompts.prompt: Using {{TARGET_IMAGE}} as the locked character, create a {{FRAME_COUNT}}-keyframe concept sequence for {{ANIMATION_TAG}}. Same camera, scale, body proportions, identity colors, facing direction and nominal center throughout; change only the moving features named in {{MOTION_DESCRIPTION}}. Show one evenly spaced row with generous flat-background gutters and no frame labels. Preserve the original silhouette's important distinguishing features. No duplicate rotors, shifting eyes, new equipment or camera motion. Keep neighboring frames visually compatible. This is a keyframe study to reconstruct and check in the sprite editor, not an automatically sliceable production atlas or a claim of fixed pivots.

prompts.intent: Export real tagged source art with traceable metadata.
reference_requirements: Existing .aseprite source.
Consumer animation/atlas contract.
prompts.prompt: Prepare a production export from the actual {{ASEPRITE_SOURCE}} according to {{ANIMATION_CONTRACT}}. Inspect existing tags, frame durations, slice pivots, canvas sizes and alpha before exporting. Preserve the editable source. Use the installed Aseprite version's documented PNG plus JSON export; include frame tags and slices, choose explicit padding and extrusion, and avoid trimming unless the consumer correctly applies offsets. Save the export command/settings and output hashes. Verify actual frame count, names, durations, bounds, transparency and pivot stability, then visually inspect a contact sheet at intended play size. If no editable sprite source or Aseprite runtime is present, report that exact missing prerequisite and deliver the command plan, not fictional files. This request authorizes sprite export, not game-code implementation.

prompts.intent: Test whether varied artwork hides live information.
reference_requirements: Actual composited fixture images, including nominal phone-size captures.
prompts.prompt: Review {{COMPOSITE_FIXTURES}} for actual-size readability. Locate the player, active trail, claimed boundary, fill-blocker mark, optional objective and decorative background vehicle/object in each fixture; note confusion with coordinates. Where represented, distinguish an open-field enemy, a patrol on an interior capture contour, an enemy crossing revealed ground, and a territory eroder with its warning footprint. A boundary patrol must remain readable when a new internal contour is drawn; claimed ground must not imply universal safety. Verify solid walls, terrain slowing only the player, and lethal fields use distinct shapes or materials instead of one generic red danger tile. Mark absent fixture coverage untested; do not invent enemy support. Compare dark, bright and detailed images across four theme families and pixel, flat illustration, painterly and photo styles. Check grayscale and relevant color-vision previews when tools exist; color alone is insufficient. Flag disappearing trails, picture objects resembling enemies, tiny markers, over-bright FX, clipped borders and crowded HUD. Confirm an optional full-artwork victory/gallery view does not falsely display 100% captured or obscure the achieved percentage. Propose the smallest correction through palette roles, outlines, a quiet underlay or background treatment without imposing neon across every theme. Do not claim user testing, numerical contrast measurement, collision validation or device testing unless actually performed.

prompts.intent: Wrap one unchanged game fixture in varied device art.
reference_requirements: A real measured 4:3 board fixture, inspected before editing.
Chosen theme reference with assigned style role.
prompts.prompt: Edit the supplied {{MEASURED_BOARD_FIXTURE}} into a device-composition study for {{DEVICE_CONTEXT}}. Preserve the board's complete rectangular boundary, 4:3 shape, player/enemy positions, capture mask and active path. Change only surrounding shell, HUD placement and decorative context using {{THEME}}. Portrait phone: complete board above the external thumb-control deck. Landscape phone: board between control rails. Laptop/handheld/TV: controller or keyboard-friendly surrounding UI. Ultrawide: ambient side art, same arena. Do not add a perspective tilt or crop the arena to fill the display. Generated exactness is only a request; flag this result as a composition study pending measured comparison. Text slots stay blank for typography composed later.

prompts.intent: Separate mockup appeal from evidence of responsive layout.
reference_requirements: Actual image or UI layout artifacts; optional browser/device runtime.
prompts.prompt: Audit the actual layout artifacts {{LAYOUT_FILES}} at representative available viewports: 320px phone width, 390px portrait width, 667×375 landscape, tablet, 1280×800 handheld and 1280×720 desktop. For each record board bounds, aspect ratio, any clipping, visual player size, control bounds and HUD collisions. Preserve level geometry across sizes; a changed board shape is a different challenge, not a responsive crop. If these are generated images, measure them as images and explicitly state that controls and safe-area behavior are untested. If a real interface exists, exercise keyboard/controller focus and touch input where supported. Report observed pass/fail evidence and exact remaining checks. Do not invent performance, device access or passing input tests.

prompts.intent: Build a specific researched Ukrainian history pack.
reference_requirements: Named region and era; relevant museum sources discovered during execution.
prompts.prompt: Research and draft a UKRAINE ATLAS chapter for {{REGION}} during {{ERA}}. Use museum collections and primary heritage/institutional sources; record a direct source for each claimed costume, building type, material or object. Provide eight reveal-art briefs tied to one period, three collectible-object closeups, palette/material notes, pronunciation/localization terms and short optional gallery captions. Label reconstruction and uncertainty, and separate sourced fact from original composition. Avoid mixing architecture or clothing from different centuries without explaining the scene. Map challenges to current capture/collect/link primitives rather than inventing historical combat systems. Deliver editable text and a source ledger; do not generate images or claim historical authenticity has been externally reviewed.

prompts.intent: Plan a varied collection with consistent identity.
reference_requirements: Approved family/chapter bible and current asset contract.
prompts.prompt: Create a twelve-image reveal pack for {{FAMILY}} and {{CHAPTER}}. Give each image a stable proposed ID, evocative title, one-sentence subject, exact generation brief, focal anchor, palette deviation, discovery detail, gallery caption and suggested difficulty pairing. Compose a deliberate visual rhythm: three intimate scenes, three wide scenes, three object-focused compositions and three surprising reveals, all inside the chapter identity. Military packs retain invading military presence in every active-play reveal. Choose {{REVEAL_STYLE}} independently of the fixed gameplay overlay. Track each asset as planned, not generated; list required references and avoid identical scenes with only changed color. Keep image IDs separate from levels so the same art can support several challenges. For each image, distinguish active-play mask coverage from the proposed completed-gallery presentation. Plan to show the full artwork after ordinary victory while retaining the achieved capture percentage for scoring; gallery visibility does not enlarge captured territory. Treat this presentation as a proposal until implemented, and do not add unsupported fields to a valid pack. Let optional high-exposure mastery reward a separate record or medal rather than withholding the basic picture reward. Keep military content specific to military packs; cultural, retro and Coupa chapters retain their own subjects.

prompts.intent: Author compatible challenge variations with explicit dependencies.
reference_requirements: Current supported ruleset catalog and level schema.
prompts.prompt: Using {{RULESET_CATALOG}} and {{LEVEL_SCHEMA}}, draft {{LEVEL_COUNT}} levels for {{THEME_PACK}} that follow the requested chapter, medium and challenge emphasis. Begin with spatial lessons: a short closure, an L-shaped return, an understandable partition and an optional marker detour. Where supported, contrast open-field motion with patrols on changing interior capture contours, movers across revealed ground and telegraphed territory erosion; do not merely increase speed or silently treat the outer-border patrol as an interior-contour patrol. Distinguish solid walls from player-only slow terrain and lethal fields in both rule descriptions and visual cues. Read the actual registry: if a domain, terrain effect, delayed trail-strike pulse, erosion or respawn rule is absent, put it in a clearly named proposed/extension-needed section outside valid pack data. The current enemy.patrol-boundary.v1 is outer-border-only unless its versioned specification changes. Use only registered enemy/objective/effect IDs and parameter semantics. For every valid level materialize geometry, player start, enemies, markers, success conditions and reveal-image references in the current schema. Explain the selected fill policy, its blockers and the expected result of a teaching cut. Distinguish collecting by touch from capturing a marker by enclosure. Proposed medal logic, linked pairs, deterministic generators and full-artwork victory presentation require their own support; two captured markers are not a linking mechanic. Recommend preserving completed territory after a life loss in the default arcade mode, but never serialize an unsupported respawn rule. Keep the proposed full-artwork victory reward separate from the measured captured fraction. A seed is recipe provenance, not a generator or proof of reproducibility. Keep decorative image subjects separate from collision and enemy occupancy. No scripts or executable expressions in content. Run the current validator when available and report results separately from playtest evidence. Registered behavior specifications are not a running game.

prompts.intent: Specify reproducible generated challenge families.
reference_requirements: Current generator capabilities, level schema and ruleset catalog.
prompts.prompt: Draft a data-only level-generator recipe for {{CHAPTER}} using only primitives in {{RULESET_CATALOG}}. Define a seed, bounded distributions for geometry and supported enemy counts/speeds, protected starting area, objective placement constraints and difficulty tiers. Describe rejection checks for blocked starts, unreachable objectives, contradictory win conditions and excessive first-move danger. Image selection and palette must not alter collision geometry or random outcomes. Include five named seed examples as proposals, not tested outputs, and a reproducibility contract that includes generator/ruleset versions. Supply a preview/review workflow so authors can save a generated result as an editable handcrafted level. Identify anything needing simulation validation rather than hiding it in a prompt.

prompts.intent: Make tactical variation legible across themes.
reference_requirements: Supported effects and module schema.
prompts.prompt: Design nine intermission module cards using the supported effects in {{RULESET_CATALOG}}. Group into route planning, safe movement and capture rewards. For every card give neutral mechanic ID, exact effect text with units, allowed stacking, incompatible combinations, one balancing risk and equivalent names/icon concepts in FPV FRONT, UKRAINE ATLAS, 1994 FOREVER and NAVI NETWORK. Use a path preview, short visible trail protection and capture-linked recharge only if those effects exist; otherwise mark extension proposals. Keep benefits readable in one sentence and selection outside live danger. Do not invent pay-to-win progression or require real-time AI calls. Output data-ready drafts with unvalidated balance status.

prompts.intent: Cover complete UI states before generating decorative menus.
reference_requirements: Theme bible and current screen-flow decisions.
prompts.prompt: Create the UI state inventory for {{THEME}} across title, pack browser, mission select, intermission, pause, failure/retry, victory, gallery, options and editor import. For each specify primary action, keyboard/controller focus start, back behavior, touch layout, empty/loading/error/offline states and localization slots. Separate semantic layout from art tokens. Include high-contrast, reduced-motion and muted-audio appearance. Require backgrounds, panels, icons and real text as separate resources; never bake functional text into generated art. Identify which screens need large scene art and which can reuse a quiet panel skin. Deliver a state table and asset checklist, no game code or claim that UI works. Define a proposed victory-to-gallery transition that freezes hazards and reveals the complete artwork while retaining the actual captured fraction, completion time and life record as separate facts. Do not replace an 80%-quota win with a fabricated 100% capture record. Provide immediate replay and next-level actions, and separate optional mastery goals from the ordinary art reward. Include teaching states that distinguish field movers, patrols on interior capture contours, revealed-ground movers and territory eroders, plus solid-wall/player-only-slow/lethal terrain symbols. Select supported roles for actual screens and track absent mechanics as proposed/extension-needed. Include an explicit trail-failure explanation and proposed respawn feedback without claiming that those runtime events already exist.

prompts.intent: Keep Ukrainian text and business terminology readable.
reference_requirements: Actual text strings, fonts and relevant mockups.
prompts.prompt: Review {{UI_COPY_AND_MOCKUPS}} for Ukrainian and English presentation. Check Ukrainian characters including Ґ, Є, І, Ї and apostrophe forms in the actual font; inspect uppercase, punctuation, numbers and mixed Latin/Cyrillic strings. Check that longer labels do not collide with controls or shrink below the measured target. Prefer clear Ukrainian names and document transliteration choices. For Navi, use supplied official Coupa terms where relevant; distinguish fictional game value points from product claims. Flag generated gibberish as placeholder text, not a typo to preserve. Report exact strings, suggested replacements and screenshot locations. Do not claim native-speaker review unless one occurred.

prompts.intent: Build reusable promotional composition families.
reference_requirements: Accepted key art, working title and intended channels.
prompts.prompt: Create a marketing asset brief for {{THEME}} using accepted {{KEY_ART}}. Plan landscape hero, square social tile, portrait story, small library tile and wide banner with named safe areas, main subject placement, title slot and crop fallback. Treat dimensions as project briefs; verify current store requirements separately before claiming compliance. Produce three message angles: daring mastery, beautiful discoveries and tactical choices. Give five short copy variants per angle and a clean typographic hierarchy. Keep key art distinct from genuine gameplay captures. Preserve military context for FPV and explicit placeholder status for Navi. Deliver briefs and exact image-edit prompts, not fictional exported files or published advertisements.

prompts.intent: Require actual audio tools and real deliverables.
reference_requirements: Completed soundtrack brief and actual authorized audio runtime or source recordings.
prompts.prompt: Produce audio for {{SOUNDTRACK_BRIEF}} only with an available authorized audio/composition tool or supplied recordings. Inspect the brief's loop length, stem alignment, event cues and output requirements. If tools are available, create an original loop and synchronized stems, render masters plus previews, inspect duration/peak/loop joins, and report the actual listening/measurement evidence. If no audio tool is available, deliver a complete composer handoff with cue sheet, MIDI note plan where meaningful and exact missing capability; do not substitute an image or pretend written timbre descriptions are music. Keep asset IDs/event mappings theme-neutral and mark output status honestly.

prompts.intent: Check whether an apparently complete theme is actually usable.
reference_requirements: Actual pack directory, current schemas and validation commands.
prompts.prompt: Review {{PACK_PATH}} against the current schema and asset requirements. Check IDs/references, missing files, dimensions, aspect/sampling metadata, sprite tags/pivots, local font glyphs, audio metadata, theme semantic colors, image focal anchors, level dependencies and safe file paths. Separate structural checks from visual review, cultural/brand fact checking and runtime/playtest evidence. Check every supported objective has readable markers in this theme and that alternate reveal styles do not silently change game rules. Identify missing/placeholder assets explicitly. Provide a concise defects list with exact files and recommended fixes; only mark checks passed when executed. Do not describe a concept mockup as a running build. Audit enemy movement-domain claims against the current registry: an outer-border patrol is not an interior-contour patrol, and a field bouncer is not a revealed-ground mover or a territory eroder. Flag missing behavior/terrain capabilities as proposed/extension-needed rather than approving them by appearance. Verify wall, player-only slow terrain and lethal-field semantics have distinct visual symbols if supported. Where a victory/gallery design exposes the complete picture, confirm its displayed captured percentage remains the actual result; presenting the full image is separate from mask geometry and scoring. Unsupported respawn, delayed trail-strike or gallery rules must remain outside schema-valid pack fields.

prompts.intent: Explore new chapter looks without fragmenting the game identity.
prompts.prompt: Create a four-panel art-direction concept board for {{FAMILY}}. Panels explore {{VARIATION_ONE}}, {{VARIATION_TWO}}, {{VARIATION_THREE}} and {{VARIATION_FOUR}}. Keep the same described hero silhouette, semantic player/trail/hazard hierarchy and UI organization while changing scene materials, palette, reveal-art styling and collection mood. Include a large reveal-art study, one hero silhouette and three palette chips in each panel. Do not draw actual gameplay geometry or fake functional labels; leave a plain 4:3 arena-shaped placeholder for later measured composition. For military variants keep invading military equipment in the reveal-art studies. For cultural variants name distinct traditions in the brief. Original art, crisp main gameplay sprite language, broad stylistic range behind it.
variations: FPV: Daybreak pixel art / Night Signal cinematic illustration / Steel Horizon gouache / winter ink-and-pixel hybrid
Atlas: Petrykivka / Kosiv ceramics / a documented historical chapter / modern Ukrainian city design
Retro: warm bedroom / rainy game shop / analog-space poster / summer arcade

prompts.intent: Make generations reproducible and iterations explainable.
reference_requirements: Actual prompt/run metadata and existing output files.
prompts.prompt: Record a complete creation or edit run for {{ASSET_ID}}. Save the selected prompt ID/version, resolved prompt text, variables, tool/provider/model if actually reported, input reference paths and hashes, assigned reference roles, output paths and hashes, timestamps, dimensions and intended pack role. List what changed from the previous candidate, what was kept, observed defects and next smallest edit. Set status to concept_generated, normalized_candidate, validated_asset or the actual lower stage supported by evidence. Preserve accepted originals and create numbered revisions; do not overwrite the only source. Track soundtrack text as a brief, images as still concepts, and sprite sheets as unvalidated until measured. Finish with a readable side-by-side review note and links to actual outputs.
